'''Claus Kalevi Montonen''' (born 1946) is a Finnish [[theoretical physicist]],{{sfn|Montonen|2012|p=416}} most known for his work with British physicist [[David Olive]] in proposing the [[Montonen–Olive duality]].{{sfn|Montonen|Olive|1977}}

==Life==
Claus Montonen received his MSc from the [[University of Helsinki]] in 1968 and his PhD at the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1974,{{sfn|Montonen|2012|p=416}} where he was taught by David Olive before he left for CERN.{{sfn|Olive|2012|p=350}} He held research fellowships at [[University of Paris-Sud|Orsay]], [[CNRS]] and [[CERN]]. From  1974 he has held various research and teaching positions at the University of Helsinki and [[Helsinki Institute of Physics]].

===Publications===
In 1977 while at CERN Montonen, together with Olive,  made the remarkable conjecture that there should exist an electromagnetic [[Duality (mathematics)|dual theory]] in which the roles of [[magnetic monopoles]] and [[gauge bosons]] are interchanged. The [[Montonen-Olive duality]] was later found to emerge from a deeper web of dualities underlying [[M-theory]], ushering in the  [[History of string theory#1994.E2.80.932003: second superstring revolution|second superstring revolution]] of the mid 1990s, through the work of [[Ed Witten]]{{sfnm|1a1=Witten|1a2=Olive|1y=1978|2a1=Seiberg|2a2=Witten|2y=1994|3a1=Seiberg|3y=1995}} and others.{{sfn|Swansea University|2012}}
